claims.value: The frozen force field reads the Fort Butler garrison of two companies of the 28th Maine and convalescents [US] against Green's and Major's brigades [CS]; the live field reads zero. Green heard from citizens on June 27 that the fort held 300 to 500 men and five gunboats, and reported on July 3 a garrison of between 500 and a figure printed '000' in OCR, against his assaulting party of about 800. Irwin says the fort held a mixed force of 180 and that Green brought six regiments and a battery of 1,300 to 1,500; his footnote reads Green's 800 as the four regiments actually engaged and derives 1,811.
claims.rationale: Figures for different scopes from an interested report and a history; the garrison figures disagree widely. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Green described an open approach of 900 yards and a ditch 16 feet wide and 12 deep, and says the assault on the river front failed at an inner ditch his guides had not told him of. Irwin describes a square redoubt in the angle of the bayou and the river with stockades to the water, and low water exposing wide margins of batture. NPS says the ditch was unknown to the attackers and too wide to cross.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested report, a history and a summary; no map verification. The fort and ditch predate the attack, but their state on June 28 is described only by these accounts, so the phase is left unresolved.

claims.value: On June 27 Green advised against storming and proposed to turn the fort from below to annoy the transports; on July 3 he says Mouton's order of the 26th was to take possession of the fort, whose capture would have troubled the army besieging Port Hudson. Irwin says Green was sent there to attack. NPS says Mouton ordered the brigades to take Donaldsonville.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from an interested report, a history and a summary; Green's June 27 advice and the attack differ.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 324 total (US 23; CS 301), and the live field agrees. Green's statement totals 40 killed, 114 wounded and 107 missing (261), and he says he saved about 100 men by his flag of truce. Irwin repeats 261 but says 124 prisoners were counted on the gunboats and the garrison buried 69 Confederates and was still at it; the garrison lost 8 killed and 13 wounded (21) and the Princess Royal 1 killed and 2 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Porter's No. 6 report, Bullen's report (not in the inspected list), Mouton's No. 11 and Taylor's No. 10 reports, Taylor's indorsements (read, not selected), Woolsey's naval report and the Union returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Its chapters cite and quote Stickney's and Green's reports, so it is not independent of them. Green's June 27 dispatch and July 3, July 14 and October 2, 1863 reports, with his undated casualty statement (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container), are one interested Confederate family; Taylor's printed indorsements are not part of it. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
